identifiedObject.title: Apollon du type de l'"Apollon Lycien" (also called Apollon de Smyrne)
identifiedObject.institution: Musée du Louvre, Paris (Département des Antiquités grecques, étrusques et romaines)
identifiedObject.version_or_date: Roman Imperial marble (Thasos marble), c. 150 CE (2nd quarter of the 2nd century CE), after a lost Greek original of the Apollo Lykeios type attributed to Praxiteles; found at Smyrna (Izmir, Mount Pagus); former French royal collection (Versailles)
identifiedObject.match_explanation: SMK KAS1026 is a plaster cast ('Gipsafstøbning') whose SMK record names the original as ORIG111, marble, current owner Louvre, moulded by the Louvre casting workshop ('Formeri: Paris, Louvre nr. 68'), acquired 1901. The Louvre has two Apollo Lykeios-type statues in Salle 344: Ma 928 (Smyrna, serpent coiled around a tree-trunk support) and Ma 916 (composite Borghese statue, low rough trunk without a coiled serpent). The SMK photograph of KAS1026 shows the serpent coiled around the tree trunk with the same branch stubs, the same banded hair with top-knot and the same pose as the Louvre photographs of Ma 928, and does not match Ma 916. KAS1026 is therefore a cast of Ma 928. KAS1026 identifies the cast; Ma 928 identifies the original.

apollo-lykeios.geometryReviewNote: The SMK cast is 231.5 cm high gross, i.e. it includes a cast plinth beyond the 220 cm Louvre figure. The cast (made c. 1901) also preserves the marble's earlier state: the SMK photograph shows a restored left forearm and hand holding an object, whereas the Louvre records that the left forearm and genitals, restored in marble shortly after 1680, were de-restored in the mid-20th century and are now missing. Mesh bounds therefore should not be used directly; scale to the 220 cm statue height excluding the cast plinth.

identifiedObject.match_explanation: SMK's linked original ORIG1077 is a marble head in the British Museum, 'Ex Townley Coll. 1774', Roman copy after c. 430 BC, citing Smith 1892 pp.269-270 and Cook, The Townley Marbles 1985 fig. 26. BM 1805,0703.80 is the Townley (ex Lyde Browne) marble head of an Amazon mounted on a modern bust, catalogued as Sculpture 503 and described as a copy of the 5th-century BC wounded Amazon leaning on a post — i.e. the Sciarra type (SMK's related cast KAS67 is the Sciarra Amazon 'with left arm on a pillar'). The BM height of 610 mm equals the SMK cast's 61 cm, and the cast image shows the head on a bust with socle, matching 'mounted on a modern bust'. Brucciani mould no. T80. identifiedObject.version_or_date: Germain Pilon (c. 1535-1590), polychromed terracotta model, 1586 (c. 1586), made at full scale for the marble Vierge de douleur intended for the Rotonde des Valois; formerly in the lower chapel of the Sainte-Chapelle du Palais, Paris; entered the Louvre 1890
identifiedObject.match_explanation: SMK KAS1999 is a plaster cast whose SMK record names the original as ORIG2756, technique 'Terrakotta', current owner Louvre, with the history 'Frankrig, Paris, La Sainte Chapelle du Palais (til 1890)' and 'i Musée des Petits-Augustins, i Consulat og endelig i L'Ecole militaire de Saint-Cyr indtil 1890'. This matches exactly the Louvre terracotta RF 3147 (Sainte-Chapelle, Musée des Monuments français 1797, Saint-Cyr 1809, Louvre 1890), not the marble version, which has been in the church of Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis since 1802. The SMK 3D file is even named 'smk-mater-dolorosa-germain-pilon-louvre'. The cast's gross dimensions (173 x 121 x 78.5 cm) correspond closely to the terracotta's 1.77 x 1.195 x 0.815 m. KAS1999 identifies the cast; RF 3147 identifies the original.

renaissance/mater-dolorosa-smk-cast.geometryReviewNote: The original is the polychromed terracotta model, not the marble version in Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis. The terracotta is assembled from several parts completed with stucco, seated on gypsum blocks, and was later set on a circular slab (dalle circulaire); the Louvre lists separate 'accessoire' dimensions (H 0.18 m, D 0.87 m) that probably refer to this slab, and it is not stated whether the 1.77 m height includes it. The SMK cast's gross height (173 cm) is 4 cm less than the Louvre figure, suggesting the cast omits the slab; the SMK 3D file name ('hollowback') indicates the scan is hollow at the back. Do not use raw mesh bounds without checking which base elements are present.

identifiedObject.title: Mithreum de Sidon — leontocephaline statue (Kronos mithriaque / Aiôn) dedicated by Flavios Gerontios
identifiedObject.institution: Musée du Louvre, Département des Antiquités orientales (record lists current location as long-term display at Musée Bonnat-Helleu, Bayonne)
identifiedObject.version_or_date: Roman Imperial; Louvre dates it to AD 389 (Greek dedication 'in the year 500' of the Sidon era). Three D Scans gives '2nd century CE'.
identifiedObject.match_explanation: The Three D Scans turntable image (Aion_Louvre.gif) shows a nude, lion-headed, four-winged male with a serpent coiled round the body, feet together, arms at the sides, on a circular base carrying a Greek inscription ending '...ΠΑΤΗΡ ΝΟΜΙΜΟΣ...'. This matches the Louvre record exactly: 'Personnage léontocéphale (Kronos mithriaque ou Aiôn) debout sur un socle circulaire, entièrement nu, pieds joints et bras collés contre le corps ... Un serpent s'enroule autour de son corps ... Sur la base est gravée une dédicace grecque de Flavios Gerontios' (Φλ. Γερόντιος, πατὴρ νόμιμος). Three D Scans lists Location: Louvre, Material: Marble, scanned 2025 (Einstar Vega). No cast is involved; the scanned object is the ancient marble itself.

roman/aion-louvre-threedscans.geometryReviewNote: The figure stands on an integral circular inscribed base carved from the same block; the Louvre height (110 cm) describes the complete statue and presumably includes that base. Check whether the STL also includes any modern museum socle. Note the Louvre dates the piece to AD 389, not the 2nd century CE given by the scan provider, and lists its current location as Bayonne (Musée Bonnat-Helleu) although Three D Scans says it was scanned at the Louvre in 2025.
